abstract: Metabolic diseases, including obesity and diabetes, are major risk factors for cognitive impairment and dementia, yet the underlying causal mechanisms remain unclear. Here we investigate whether this link is mediated by dysfunctional changes in cerebral microvessels. Using a multimodal longitudinal approach combining 3D light-sheet fluorescence microscopy, contrast-enhanced MRI and cognitive testing, we characterise structural, functional and behavioural changes to the brain microvasculature in a mixed-sex mouse model of diet-induced obesity (DIO). Our results reveal a striking sex-specific vulnerability to obesity-driven cerebrovascular dysfunction. Brains from male DIO mice exhibited reduced capillary diameter and volume in the frontal cortex, alongside decreased blood volume and accelerated cognitive decline over time in an object recognition task. Conversely, female DIO mice displayed compensatory capillary vasodilation and were protected against neurovascular and cognitive impairment. These findings link cerebral microvascular changes to obesity-associated cognitive decline, and identify sex-dependent differences in the cerebrovascular response to obesity.
